title: Disjoint file partitions let subagents implement ticket waves in parallel
summary: Partitioning a multi-ticket implementation wave so each subagent owns a disjoint file set allowed six parallel workers with zero real conflicts; pair this with red-then-green it.fails tests and prefer removing an unnecessary credential requirement over loosening a binding.
hint_triggers: MSN-CLI-RELIABILITY-M1-20261031 implemented tickets R02-R16 with six parallel subagents, each assigned a disjoint file partition; the only overlap was a single commit sweep with content preserved. The it.fails tests pinned in R01 were flipped to green by the real R03 fix, and R03 was resolved by removing an unnecessary credential requirement from lifecycle-verb reasoning bootstrap rather than loosening the binding. Lesson: for ticket-wave implementation, declare disjoint file ownership per subagent up front and record per-ticket diffs so later distillation can attribute causes.
